newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel rabbi says Jews out of Hebron if unsafe.
newsitem.headline: Israel rabbi says Jews out of Hebron if unsafe.

text.p: Israel's Chief Sephardic Rabbi said Jewish settlers should evacuate the West Bank town of Hebron if Israel could not guarantee their security.
A spokesman on Tuesday confirmed remarks attributed to Rabbi Eliahu Bakshi-Doron while touring Hebron, where 400 Jewish settlers live amid 100,000 Palestinians.

"It is preferable that Jews remain in Hebron, but if it is impossible to ensure their security there, it is forbidden for them to remain and live there," Bakshi-Doron was quoted as saying by the newspaper Maariv.

"Preservation of life supersedes everything -- including the religious commandment of settling the land," the rabbi was quoted as saying. Religious Jews view the West Bank, occupied by Israel since 1967, as biblical Israel promised them by God.

Hebron, holy to Moslems and Jews as the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham, is the most sensitive of seven West Bank towns Israel agreed to turn over to the Palestinians under a 1995 peace deal.

It is a flashpoint of violence. In February 1994 Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from Kiryat Arba settlement adjacent to Hebron, shot dead 29 Arabs at prayer in the tomb, also known as al-Ibrahimi mosque. Survivors beat him to death.
Israeli and PLO negotiators are locked in talks on a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeks to modify a Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous government to safeguard the settlers in the heart of it.
Palestinians reject any changes to the deal.

The spokesman also confirmed remarks by Israel's Chief Ashkenazic Rabbi Yisrael Meir Lau, who called on Jewish zealots not to forcefully oppose Israeli troops ordered to hand over parts of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

"I call with all my heart on the (Hebron) residents that heaven forbid they will get the idea to raise a hand against a soldier or policeman who comes to do his duty. The people of Hebron must obey the law," Maariv quoted Lau as saying.
Lau represents Ashkenazic Jews of European origin and Bakshi-Doron is the chief cleric for Israel's Sephardic Jews, who mainly come from Middle East and North African countries.

Israel's Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said over the weekend Israel would detain dozens of Jewish militants who might actively oppose a turnover of Hebron. He said such "extremists" might try to open fire.
